Consequently, coordinates of the centered target split into independent Gaussian blocks with the stated covariances. This is an exact identity, with no approximation/error and no statement limited to densities, moments, support, or one chosen event.
The residual covariance is the identity, since the residual precision is the identity.
The fixed-tuple factorization is a prerequisite of the printed averaged Eq6, not a proof of Eq6 by itself.

Conditional here means the Gaussian kernel evaluated at a fixed parameter tuple, before prior integration; the raw scope does not authorize replacing a pointwise identity by an unspecified almost-everywhere regular conditional representative.

All matrices are real, transpose is the Euclidean transpose, and the covariance is the inverse of the full literal precision. A diagonal-vector substitute or an independently supplied covariance is insufficient without an audited equivalence to that precision.
The claim concerns the source centered Gaussian, including its actual covariance, not simply a law declared Gaussian by a bundled hypothesis.
The source regularity facts I_n<=A_O<=kappa I_n and I_d<=A_boldO<=kappa I_d provide positivity/invertibility internally. No source theorem separately names the fixed-tuple product producer.
The target f_A(x)=(1/2)x^T A x has its source minimum at zero. That regularity conclusion is relevant source context but is not an additional assumption for the fixed Gaussian product law.
There are no unspecified multiplicative constants in the fixed-law equality.
The exact coefficients (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4 are fixed by Eq4; the associated cross-term coefficient in Ex73 is (kappa-1)/2.
k depends on d,n by floor(d/n); r=d-kn. No query budget T, determinant sign b, prior distribution, error epsilon, or hidden dimension-dependent constant enters the fixed-tuple identity.
